title: Program Manager III, Transportation Financial Systems (TFS)
description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

Transportation Financial Systems (TFS) team is looking for a talented and highly motivated Sr. Program Manager who enjoy solving challenging and complex business problems at Amazon scale.  
  
Imagine being a part of a team where every single team member is a critical voice in the decision-making process, has a meaningful impact on product features, and has the ability to re-define the customer experience. Welcome to Transportation Financial Systems (TFS), where we are building multiple financial automation products and functionalities to meet Amazon’s ever-growing finance and accounting customer requirements. You will be in a well-funded, highly technical, and highly visible business critical tech platform team.  
  
We are a technology team focused on building a suite of products for transportation financial systems and beyond that enable Amazon business units (BUs) to add new offerings at scale. Our products abstract complexities from the world of accounting, invoicing, audit, payment, taxation, and allocation at the required level of fidelity and insights to build generic solutions scalable to multiple businesses and geographies. We ensure that financial functions are complete, accurate, timely and compliant with worldwide regulatory and tax requirements. Our software systems include services that handle thousands or requests per second and make decisions to pay billions of dollars a year and ensure that transportation's liabilities and revenues are correctly accounted. Our current team comprises of ~200+ engineering organization and Program management team of 10+ TPMs and Program Managers with great growth and lateral opportunity.  
  
We are looking for a high caliber Senior Program Manager (Sr. PM) who enjoy working on challenging, high impact business problems. The Sr. PM will manage business onboarding to our systems and services, prioritize opportunities in tech systems /process flows and support the functional systems to deliver to defined goals. Successful candidates will be analytical, highly-organized, accustomed to working with technical teams, able to bridge the gap between business and tech, clear communicators, and interested in getting deep into the details of our business. This Program Manager is a high visible role as s/he will front end with Senior Leaders across Amazon Organization.  
  
Key job responsibilities  
As a Sr. PM on the team, you would be responsible for understanding the functional flow of TFS onboarded businesses and key TFS capabilities, required to enable transport finance processes (account payables and receivables) and identifying opportunities to refine both. The Sr. PM will manage the auditing, invoicing, payments products and process with a team of SMEs in TFS and partner teams, identify short term solutions and work with Product/SDM on long term solutions to customer problems. The Sr. PM will evaluate self-serve opportunities to reduce overhead load on TFS, document dashboard or tool requirements and present to TFS Tech team to build consensus for solutions to self-serve on commonly occurring issues. The program manager will work closely with Product/SDM to define the road map. Key responsibilities -
  
  

* Define and manage cross-functional program strategy, including mission, vision, objectives, and measurable success criteria, while driving teams across organizations to deliver on key milestones.
* Analyze data to identify trends, drive improvements, and inform resource allocation decisions — regularly reviewing metrics and proactively seeking new mechanisms for visibility into program health.
* Lead stakeholder alignment through clear written narratives and verbal communication, presenting program updates, trade-offs, and recommendations to senior leadership.
* Identify and mitigate risks proactively, reduce exposure to common failure modes such as unclear requirements or ineffective cross-team collaboration, and solve ambiguous problems with sound judgment.
* Streamline processes and eliminate unnecessary dependencies, partnering with engineering and business teams to prioritize initiatives that improve efficiency and customer outcomes.

  
A day in the life  
TFS has over 200+ engineers, and 20+ product & program managers. Each Program Manager is responsible for delivering large to medium programs; working closely with business teams and product, building transformation roadmaps to deliver long term benefits for our customers.  
  
About the team  
Transportation Financial Systems (TFS) platform owns the technology components that perform the financial activities for Amazon’s transportation business. TFS systems are used across all Amazon’s transportation programs and retail expansion to new geographies. The platform provide financial document creation & management, expense auditing, accounting, payments and cost allocation functions. Our new generation products are highly scalable and operate at finer level granularity to reconcile every dollar in transportation financial accounts with zero manual entries or corrections. The goal is to develop global product suite for all freight modes touching every single package movement across Amazon. Our mission is to abstract logistics complexities from financial world and financial complexities from logistics world. You will be part of one of the largest tech and program team with ~200 engineering organization with great growth and lateral opportunity.

**BASIC QUALIFICATIONS**
------------------------

* 5+ years of program or project management experience
* Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
* Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
* Experience owning program strategy, end-to-end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**
----------------------------

* 5+ years of driving process improvements experience
* Master's degree, or MBA in business, operations, human resources, adult education, organizational development, instructional design or related field

  
Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations for more information. description:
The Infrastructure Change & Release Manager is responsible for governing, coordinating, and continuously improving the end to end Change Enablement and Release Management processes across enterprise IT infrastructure.  
The role ensures that infrastructure changes and releases are properly assessed, authorized, scheduled, communicated, implemented, and reviewed, while minimizing business disruption and maintaining service availability.  
The position works closely with Infrastructure Operations, Cloud, Network, Database, Security, Application, Service Management, Project/Program Management, and business teams.  
  
Key Responsibilities  
1. Change Management / Change Enablement  
  
. Own and manage the enterprise Change Management / Change Enablement process.  
. Review infrastructure RFCs for completeness, technical readiness, risk, impact, dependencies, implementation plans, testing evidence, rollback plans, and business approvals.  
. Classify and manage: Standard Changes Normal Changes Emergency Changes  
. Facilitate Change Advisory Board (CAB) and, where required, Emergency CAB (ECAB) meetings.  
. Ensure high risk and business critical changes receive appropriate technical and business approvals.  
. Maintain the enterprise Change Calendar / Forward Schedule of Change (FSC).  
. Identify scheduling conflicts between infrastructure, application, security, maintenance, and release activities.  
. Coordinate changes across technologies including: Windows/Linux VMware/virtualization Azure/AWS/cloud infrastructure Network and firewall Database Storage and backup Middleware End user computing Cybersecurity infrastructure  
. Ensure changes comply with organizational governance, audit, security, and regulatory requirements.  
  
  
2. Release Management  
  
. Plan and coordinate infrastructure releases from development/testing through production deployment.  
. Develop and maintain release calendars and deployment schedules.  
. Coordinate release readiness across infrastructure, application, security, testing, operations, and business stakeholders.  
. Ensure releases have: Defined implementation plans Deployment sequencing Testing and validation evidence Business/service owner approval Communication plans Backout/rollback procedures Post deployment validation  
. Manage release dependencies across multiple technology platforms.  
. Coordinate major releases, infrastructure upgrades, migrations, patching programs, and transformation initiatives.  
. Ensure appropriate handover into BAU/Operations following deployment.  
  
  
3. Risk & Impact Management  
Perform or facilitate assessment of changes based on factors such as:  
  
. Business impact  
. Technical complexity  
. Service criticality  
. Number of affected users  
. Application/service dependencies  
. Implementation duration  
. Previous change history  
. Security implications  
. Customer impact  
. Rollback complexity  
  
Challenge high risk changes where implementation, testing, communication, or rollback arrangements are insufficient.  
  
4. CAB Governance  
Plan, chair, and govern CAB meetings.  
Typical responsibilities include:  
  
1. Review upcoming changes.  
2. Highlight high risk and high impact changes.  
3. Validate implementation and rollback readiness.  
4. Identify scheduling conflicts.  
5. Verify stakeholder approvals.  
6. Review business/service impact.  
7. Approve, reject, defer, or escalate changes in accordance with delegated authority.  
8. Track actions and decisions.  
9. Review failed and backed out changes.  
10. Ensure emergency changes are retrospectively reviewed.  
  
  
5. Major & Emergency Changes  
  
. Coordinate urgent infrastructure changes required to restore services or mitigate significant operational/security risk.  
. Facilitate ECAB approvals where required.  
. Ensure emergency procedures do not bypass essential technical and risk controls.  
. Coordinate with Major Incident Management during service restoration activities.  
. Ensure retrospective documentation and review of emergency changes.  
. Identify repeated emergency changes and drive appropriate problem management or automation improvements.  
  
  
6. Post Implementation Review  
Conduct or coordinate Post Implementation Reviews (PIRs) for:  
  
. Failed changes  
. Backed out changes  
. High risk changes  
. Changes resulting in incidents  
. Major releases  
. Emergency changes, where required

title: Project Coordinator – YCLC (Kolar - Karnataka)
description:
**Job Profile:**

**1. About Bindi International**

Bindi International Association is a grassroots organisation working at the intersection of education, gender equity, community wellbeing and climate action. The organisation works with underserved communities across India to strengthen access to education, build local leadership and enable communities to participate in sustainable development.

**2. About the Programme**

The Young Climate Leadership Curriculum (YCLC) aims to equip children and young people with the knowledge, skills and confidence to understand climate change and participate in meaningful climate action. Under the Climate Smart Communities initiative, YCLC connects climate education with practical interventions in schools and communities, helping students understand local environmental challenges, explore sustainable solutions and engage in collective action.

**The programme follows the Think–Speak–Act approach:**

- Think: Build understanding of climate change, environmental sustainability and locally relevant climate issues.

- Speak: Encourage students to express their perspectives, discuss solutions and communicate with peers and communities.

- Act: Enable students to lead climate action initiatives and campaigns within their schools and communities.

Climate Fellows will directly implement the curriculum in schools and facilitate student activities.

The Project Coordinator will provide leadership, coordination, mentoring and quality assurance to ensure effective implementation across 20 government schools and their surrounding communities.

**3. Role Overview**

The Project Coordinator will be responsible for the overall field-level implementation and coordination of YCLC across 20 government schools and their surrounding communities in Karnataka. The coordinator will manage and support Climate Fellows who will deliver curriculum sessions and facilitate student-led activities in schools. The role will involve developing implementation plans, coordinating with school authorities, mentoring fellows, monitoring programme quality and enabling students to translate climate learning into practical action.

The coordinator will also lead community engagement and support the planning and implementation of climate action campaigns involving students, Climate Fellows, teachers, families and community stakeholders. The position requires a proactive, field-oriented professional who can manage multiple stakeholders, ensure accountability for programme delivery and help build a culture of climate awareness, leadership and action across participating schools and communities.

**4. Key Responsibilities**

A. Programme Planning and School Coordination

- Lead the implementation of YCLC across 20 government schools in Karnataka through the Climate Fellows.

- Develop school-wise implementation plans, activity calendars and targets aligned with the approved programme work plan.

- Coordinate with school heads, teachers and relevant education authorities to facilitate programme approvals, scheduling and implementation.

- Establish clear school allocations, responsibilities and timelines for Climate Fellows.

- Ensure that fellows have the curriculum, facilitation guides, teaching materials and resources required for effective delivery.

- Conduct regular school visits to monitor implementation, observe selected sessions and address field-level challenges.

- Maintain an overview of programme progress across all 20 schools and take timely corrective action when implementation gaps arise.

**B. Climate Fellow Management, Mentoring and Support**

- Coordinate and oversee the work of Climate Fellows responsible for implementing YCLC in assigned schools.

- Orient fellows on the curriculum, Think–Speak–Act approach, climate education concepts, facilitation techniques and expected programme outcomes.

- Develop clear work plans and implementation targets for fellows, including school visits, curriculum sessions, student activities and community engagement.

- Conduct regular review meetings to track progress, discuss challenges and identify solutions.

- Provide ongoing mentoring, feedback and field-level support to strengthen fellows’ facilitation and coordination skills.

- Conduct periodic observations of curriculum sessions and provide constructive feedback on quality, student participation and learning.

- Monitor fellows’ attendance, field activities, session completion, documentation and reporting.

- Identify capacity-building needs and coordinate refresher training and peer-learning opportunities.

- Encourage fellows to share effective practices, local innovations and implementation learning across schools.

**C. Curriculum Implementation and Student Climate Leadership**

- Ensure that Climate Fellows implement the YCLC curriculum consistently while contextualising activities to local environmental issues and students’ lived experiences.

- Monitor the use of the Think–Speak–Act approach to strengthen critical thinking, communication, participation and action among students.

- Support fellows in facilitating classroom discussions, group activities, experiential learning, student projects and climate leadership exercises.

- Help students identify environmental challenges in their schools and communities and explore practical solutions.

- Connect classroom learning with relevant climate-smart interventions, such as solar electrification, composting, tree plantation, biodiversity conservation, beekeeping and green livelihood initiatives, where applicable.

- Encourage students to become climate leaders and ambassadors who can share their learning, mobilise peers and contribute to community-level change.

- Identify opportunities to strengthen student participation, creativity, ownership and leadership throughout programme implementation.

D. Community Engagement and Climate Action Campaigns

- Lead community engagement across the 20 participating schools and their surrounding

communities, working with Climate Fellows to connect climate education with local environmental priorities.

- Engage parents, community leaders, teachers, local institutions and other stakeholders in programme activities and climate action initiatives.

- Support Climate Fellows and students in identifying local climate and environmental challenges and translating their learning into practical, community-led action.

- Plan, coordinate and monitor climate action campaigns led by students and Climate Fellows on issues such as waste management, plastic reduction, water conservation, tree plantation, biodiversity, renewable energy and other locally relevant climate priorities.

- Enable students to design and participate in school-based and community-level campaigns, including awareness drives, rallies, action days, community meetings, pledges and practical environmental initiatives.

- Encourage students to mobilise peers, families and community members to participate in climate-positive actions.

- Build partnerships with schools, community groups, local institutions and relevant stakeholders to strengthen campaign participation and continuity.

- Connect campaigns with existing climate-smart interventions, including solar energy, composting, plantation, beekeeping and green livelihood initiatives, where relevant.

- Promote opportunities for students to share their climate learning with families and communities and encourage collective problem-solving.

- Document campaign participation, actions undertaken, community responses and outcomes to demonstrate programme progress.

- Ensure that campaigns move beyond awareness generation towards tangible climate action, community participation and sustained environmentally responsible practices.

**E. Monitoring, Evaluation and Programme Quality**

- Develop and maintain systems to track implementation across all 20 schools and their associated communities.

- Consolidate school-wise and fellow-wise progress data, including sessions conducted, student participation, activities completed and campaign implementation.

- Conduct regular field visits to verify reported progress and assess curriculum delivery and programme quality.

- Coordinate baseline and endline assessments, student feedback and other monitoring activities as required.

- Track progress against programme indicators and identify gaps requiring additional support or corrective action.

- Monitor the participation of students, teachers and community members in climate education and action initiatives.

- Use monitoring findings to strengthen implementation quality, improve student engagement and inform programme decisions.

- Ensure timely, accurate and complete reporting from Climate Fellows.

**F. Documentation, Reporting and Learning**

- Prepare regular programme progress reports for the Programme Lead or designated Programme Manager.

- Maintain updated school-wise implementation trackers, fellow activity records, attendance registers and documentation of programme activities.

- Document student-led climate action campaigns, community initiatives, local solutions and examples of emerging climate leadership.

- Capture case studies, student voices, field experiences and lessons learned from programme implementation.

- Document challenges, adaptations and effective practices that can inform future programme improvements.

- Ensure that photographs, stories and other documentation involving children are collected and used in accordance with safeguarding, consent and organisational policies.

- Contribute to programme reviews, presentations, donor reporting and other communication requirements as needed.

**G. Stakeholder Coordination and Programme Operations**

- Maintain regular communication with school authorities, Climate Fellows, community stakeholders, implementation partners and the central programme team.

- Coordinate training sessions, review meetings, school activities, community campaigns and programme events.

- Ensure timely distribution and appropriate use of curriculum materials and other programme resources.

- Manage field schedules, travel, logistics and activity-related documentation in accordance with approved budgets and organisational procedures.

- Maintain relevant administrative records and supporting documentation for programme expenditure.

- Adhere to organisational safeguarding, child protection, inclusion and ethical engagement standards in all school and community activities.

**6. Qualifications and Experience**

- Bachelor’s degree in Education, Environmental Studies, Climate Science, Social Sciences, Development Studies or a related discipline. Relevant practical experience may be considered.

- Approximately 2–4 years of experience in programme coordination, education, climate action, community development or youth engagement.

- Experience coordinating field teams, fellows, facilitators or community-based programme personnel.

- Experience working with government schools, teachers, children and rural communities will be an advantage.

- Familiarity with climate change, environmental sustainability, renewable energy, environmental education or community-led climate action.

- Experience organising awareness campaigns, community events, student activities or local action initiatives is desirable.

- Proficiency in Kannada and English. Knowledge of other languages relevant to the project geography will be an advantage.

- Willingness to travel regularly to participating schools and communities across the assigned geography.

**7. Key Skills and Competencies**

- Team management and mentoring: Ability to guide, motivate and support Climate Fellows to achieve programme targets.

- Field coordination: Strong planning, scheduling, implementation tracking and problem-solving

**skills.**

- School and community engagement: Ability to build relationships with school authorities, teachers, families and community stakeholders.

- Climate education: Interest in climate change, environmental sustainability and locally relevant climate solutions.

- Campaign planning: Ability to coordinate participatory campaigns and translate programme objectives into practical activities.

- Monitoring and documentation: Ability to maintain accurate records, analyse implementation progress and prepare reports.

- Communication and facilitation: Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work collaboratively with diverse stakeholders.

- Ownership and accountability: Ability to manage multiple priorities, work independently and maintain regular communication with programme leadership.

- Child-centred approach: Commitment to inclusive learning, student participation, safeguarding and enabling young people to exercise leadership.

**8. What We Are Looking For**

We are looking for a proactive and accountable professional who believes that climate education must extend beyond awareness to meaningful participation and action. The ideal candidate will be able to support and guide Climate Fellows, build strong relationships with schools and communities, and ensure that students have opportunities to identify local environmental challenges and take action to address them.

They should combine strong implementation and team coordination skills with an understanding of community realities, a collaborative working style and a commitment to building climate-smart communities through education and youth leadership.

**9. Application Process**

Interested candidates should submit their updated CV to recruitment@bindi-international.org with subject line- Program Coordinator, young climate leadership curriculum -CSC and a brief cover note highlighting their relevant experience in programme coordination, team management, school engagement, climate education or community-led initiatives.

**₹45,000 per month**

description:
Sprinklr is the definitive, AI-native platform for Unified Customer Experience Management (Unified-CXM), empowering brands to deliver extraordinary experiences at scale — across every customer touchpoint.

Today, 1,900+ enterprises and 60% of the Fortune 100 rely on Sprinklr to help them deliver consistent, trusted customer experiences worldwide.

**Job Description**
-------------------

**Role summary**

We are hiring a Principal Program Manager to run global programs for our SDR (Sales Development) and ISR (Inside Sales Rep) teams. This role drives outcomes across productivity, pipeline quality, hygiene, win rate, NAAR, retention, and expansion by building a strong operating rhythm, using data to spot issues early, and ensuring teams execute consistently.

You may not have direct reporting lines, but you will lead through influence and partner closely with Sales Leadership, RevOps, Enablement, Marketing, Customer Success/Renewals, Finance, and Systems teams.

**Key outcomes you will drive**

* Productivity: activity effectiveness, meetings created, pipeline generated, ramp speed
* Hygiene: CRM/data discipline, stage accuracy, clean handoffs and follow-ups
* Quality: better qualification, better account/persona targeting, higher quality pipeline
* Win rate: improved conversion through the funnel and better deal outcomes
* NAAR: focus on opportunities that drive higher revenue impact
* Retention: fewer churn risks through early signals and strong renewal execution
* Expansion: stronger upsell/cross-sell pipeline and execution in existing accounts

**What you will own**

**Global programs (SDR and ISR)**

* Design and run global programs that improve productivity, quality, hygiene, win rate, and NAAR outcomes.
* Set simple standards and targets by region/segment and drive weekly follow-through across time zones.
* Create playbooks that make execution consistent (account selection, persona targeting, messaging, qualification, and handoffs).

**Retention and expansion programs (ISR focus)**

* Build programs that improve renewals, retention, and expansion outcomes (upsell and cross-sell).
* Create simple ways to track renewal health and identify churn risk early (low adoption, unresolved issues, sponsor change, engagement drop).
* Drive consistent cadences for renewal forecasting and expansion pipeline, with clear action plans and owners.
* Partner with Customer Success and Renewals teams to improve handoffs, coverage, and account planning.

**Operating rhythm and executive governance**

* Run weekly/monthly cadences: productivity reviews, hygiene reviews, quality reviews, win rate reviews, and renewal/expansion reviews.
* Create clear dashboards and short weekly readouts for senior leaders: what changed, why it changed, and what actions are needed.
* Drive accountability by tracking actions, deadlines, and measurable outcomes.

**Analytics, reporting, process, and tools**

* Build and maintain trusted reporting using Excel/Google Sheets and dashboards; SQL/BI (Tableau/Power BI) is a plus.
* Strengthen the basics: CRM hygiene, funnel definitions, stage discipline, attribution, and forecasting inputs.
* Partner with Systems/RevOps teams to improve tool adoption and workflow efficiency (e.g., Salesforce, Outreach/Salesloft, Gong, ZoomInfo).
* Use data to identify where the funnel breaks and drive targeted enablement with leaders (messaging, discovery, objection handling, deal coaching).

**Cross-functional leadership (drive without authority)**

* Align SDR/ISR leaders, AEs, Customer Success, Renewals, Marketing, Enablement, and RevOps on shared goals and execution plans.
* Remove blockers, drive decisions, and ensure teams adopt the programs and standards.
* Communicate clearly and confidently with senior stakeholders across regions.

**Required qualifications**

* 15+ years of experience, including meaningful experience in SaaS sales.
* Must have been an SDR and/or AE earlier in your career (quota-carrying experience required).
* Proven experience leading global sales programs that drive measurable outcomes (productivity, hygiene, quality, win rate, NAAR impact).
* Experience with existing-business motions: renewals, retention, and expansion (upsell and cross-sell).
* Strong analytical capability and comfort with funnel analysis and executive-ready reporting.
* Strong understanding of RevOps-level fundamentals: process rigor, definitions, hygiene, forecasting inputs, and operating cadence (title not required).
* Strong executive communication and ability to influence leaders across geographies and time zones.

**We focus on our mission**: Sprinklr was founded in 2009 to solve a big problem: growing enterprise complexity that separated brands from their customers. * Lead a new category of enterprise software that we call Unified-CXM.

* Empower companies to deliver next generation, unified engagement journeys that reimagine the customer experience.
* Create a culture of customer obsession, with trust, teamwork, and accountability.

**We believe in our product**: Customers who value exceptional customer experiences have what they need on our single unified platform, built with an operating system approach on a single codebase. That means that everything — and everyone — can work together to service, respond, sell, and market to customers on the channels they prefer. While Unified Customer Experience Management (Unified-CXM) as a category is just getting started, we are well on our way to creating a no-compromise, unified approach to better customer experiences for the world’s leading enterprise brands.

**We invest in our people**: We offer a comprehensive suite of benefits designed to help each member of our team thrive. We fervently believe every employee matters and should be respected and heard. We believe we are stronger when we belong because collectively, we’re more innovative, creative, and successful.

Job Description \- Construction Manager (PDS)
  
  

Construction Manager
  
Project and Development Services – Corporate Solutions (region/country)
  
  

**What this job involves:**  

Being the backbone of construction projects
  
You’ll oversee all day\-to\-day construction\-related projects onsite and make sure that all budget, risk, schedule, design, safety and quality management requirements are met. As the go\-to person in all construction activities, you’ll help fix any issues that may arise—all while taking heed of clients’ expectations and the company’s procedures. Your task is to ensure all site contractors involved in the project are working on all counts and with telling effect. As needed, you will also cooperate with LDI and the client to monitor, review and resolve any site\-related issues. Using the JLL Atlas platform, you’ll set up site procedures to ensure the program, cost, design, safety and quality are aligned. You’ll also be responsible for holding internal and external construction meetings.
  
Planning successful outcomes
  
As a construction manager, a thoughtful deliverable strategy is your weapon. You’ll need to prepare a master construction schedule for site as well as client and tracking. Part of regular checklist is to review all pending issues with the site team to steer clear of any communication gaps and develop action plans as soon as possible. You’ll also conduct weekly site and report meetings with consultants, contractors and agencies to review the progress per agreed schedule and proactively follow up on all pending issues. Likewise, you’ll review the site’s progress payments to make sure claims from subcontractors reflect the actual progress.
  
Mastering technical management and communication
  
In this role, you’ll take the lead and track the progress of coordination drawings submitted by local design consultants, and to get a hold of and follow up drawings, details or clarifications, as needed. You’ll then need to review these drawings to make sure they’re foolproof. You’ll also manage the technical handover and the client’s sign off at the end of a project. Equally, you’ll review the work method statement from subcontractors. On top of these, you’ll also review VOs and make sure they’re valid; set up the site diary and record system; and other duties, as directed.
  
Clearing safety and quality hurdles
  
This role calls for a champion for safety and quality management. Part of your responsibilities is to review the RFP documentation from a constructability point of view, provide the work scope; make sure that you go over safe work method statements by Janli; hold safety meetings on a weekly basis; take care of monthly health and safety reports; and make sure that the construction works match the client’s expectations.
  
  

**Sound like you? To apply you need to be:**  

Seasoned and credentialed
  
You have a degree in architectural, civil engineering, MEP engineering, or related discipline or field, or a mix of formal education and work experience of more than five years. Experience in construction site management is a must. You should also have completed safety trainings and must have acquired construction estimation skills.

A strong understanding of all aspects of development management—including financial, appraisal, risk management, and negotiation, among others—is required for this role. You should also have the know\-how of interpreting, coordinating and discussing construction drawings. As construction manager, design contracts and commercial negotiations should already be second nature to you. Also indispensable in this role is your ability to sit in on market analyses and marketing processes.
  
An excellent communicator
  
To excel in this role, you should have a superb communication skills, which will be helpful to you in winning businesses with both international and domestic clients. Your great communication skills will also serve as a tool in inspiring your members and contractors; keeping healthy client relationships alive; making headways in promoting a culture of openness; and bringing on project success stories.

Apply today!
